purpose: Instruction/allocation evidence for selected optimization stages and final Rust ThinLTO references; elapsed-time benchmark results are recorded separately.
method_limits: Callgrind measures executed machine instructions, not hardware CPU cycles, cache misses, or wall-time fractions. Instructions have different costs; REP/copy counts and uncontended atomic operations particularly must not be treated as elapsed-time shares.
DHAT replaces allocator routines and reports requested bytes, allocation blocks, peak live allocations, and lifetimes. These are not allocator-reserved bytes or process RSS.
Profiling runs may overlap independent build work. Instrumented elapsed times are deliberately excluded; clean whole-process timing uses a separate benchmark record.
Inlining moves work from runtime function entries into callers. Fewer named runtime calls alone does not prove less semantic work.
The selected Imre stages are cumulative, but the decoded-access stage also enables and tunes cross-language ThinLTO; that stage is not a single-change ablation.

Rust BigInt preserves arbitrary-precision value semantics; the checked-i64 reference has a narrower integer contract. Both captured workloads fit its range. Rust uses native indices where the algorithm guarantees valid container lengths.

Every run preserves and verifies complete stdout bytes, empty stderr, successful exit, and binary hashes. Full raw traces, logs, output, and build snapshots remain in ignored local evidence directories; this compact file records their hashes.

Both default-budget and matched-budget Rust ThinLTO controls are retained. The matched controls explicitly use import-instr-limit=1000 and inline-threshold=1000, matching the tuned Imre stages; inherited encoded flags are unset.
These two 16,384-task workloads characterize this program and environment, not general Python or Rust performance.

stages.description: Baseline plus allocation-free tagged-small decimal parsing
Parser plus conservative local tuple scalar replacement
Tuple stage plus inline short-string storage
Short strings plus decoded indices, selective runtime inlining, and tuned cross-language ThinLTO
Decoded ThinLTO stage plus inline fixed fields for up to four slots
Inline-field stage plus direct itoa/byte output, retaining the original Mutex; preserved precommit ablation build
Exact clean-worktree Imre binary used in the final matched-budget five-way timing comparison

pop_ready_normal_region.identification: Inferred from exact binary disassembly: starts at ready[0], includes pop and sift-down, ends before order.append. This is the normal executed region, not all outlined failure/BigInt paths.
pop_ready_normal_region.tag_test_scope: Counts only executed test/and $1 instructions within the region; other tag checks and their branches are not included.

limitations: All counts are machine instructions, not CPU cycles or elapsed-time shares. Inclusive costs overlap and must not be summed.

The normal heap region repeatedly decodes tags, normalizes signed indices, updates/checks RefCell borrow state, checks bounds, and tests loaded value tags. These checks remain semantically necessary unless the compiler proves stronger facts.
This supports an optimization direction, not a claim that the entire measured Rust time gap is caused by these operations. Existing local/parameter borrowing is already enabled.

attribution_notes: Small decimal parsing removes all observed parser allocation stacks: 165,021 blocks on layered input and 49,155 on wide input.
Local tuple scalarization removes 65,536 blocks and 2,883,584 requested bytes on each input; whole-tuple escapes retain the boxed fallback.
Compact strings remove all split-token character-buffer allocations: 71,391 layered and 32,769 wide. Each token retains its Rc owner.
Decoded indices plus tuned ThinLTO remove separate list get/set/len and fixed-field get/set calls from these traces; sequence get remains for 38,622 layered accesses.

Inline fixed fields remove 16,386 allocation blocks per workload and lower peak live bytes by 130,944, but increase total requested bytes by 524,480 because shared sequence headers grow from 56 to 96 bytes.

Direct byte/itoa output retains the Mutex. The exact final measured build uses 19,635,900 fewer layered and 18,292,238 fewer wide instructions than the inline-fields stage. Allocation totals are unchanged. The earlier direct-output ablation is retained separately; its counts differ from the clean final rebuild by only 59 instructions per workload.
The compiler already borrows unchanged parameters and direct local operands. Those existing optimizations are not counted as new opportunities here.
